title: Use of sNfL (serum neurofilament light chain) as a biomarker in MS (multiple sclerosis) in care (NeuroFilMS)
summary:
Biomarkers indicate disease processes in blood or tissue samples and can provide information about the course of the disease or the response to therapy.
As part of this study project, we would like to investigate the biomarker neurofilament light chain protein. It is a special protein that occurs in the nerve fibers of the brain and spinal cord. When nerve cells are damaged, e.g. in MS, NfL is released into the blood (serum). An increased sNfL value can therefore indicate nerve damage and a reduced value during the course of the disease can indicate a response to therapy.

Until now, the disease activity of MS has primarily  been assessed on the basis of the number and severity of relapses (occurrence of signs of the disease) and the activity in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). With the MRI new or enlarged area of inflammation in the brain or spinal cord can be detected, indicating increased disease activity.

interventions.name:
To participate in the study, patients must be at least 18 years old and either have been receiving stable DMD for at least 6 months, have not received DMD for at least 6 months or be considered new patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Written declaration of consent for participation in the study on the use of sNfL in healthcare practice
• Written declaration of consent for the ms register
• Relapsing MS (RMS) -> active SPMS and RRMS 
• DMT stable for 6 month or no therapy for 6 months
• Inclusion possible directly after diagnosis
• No traumatic brain injury (TBI) or serious accident in the last 3 months
Exclusion criteria:
no relapsing-remitting course of ms
